novelty_flags.one_line: The proposal says Squires et al.'s Assumption 1 recovers only the transitive closure and reserves full-DAG recovery for perfect interventions, but its Theorem 1 states recovery of G under Assumption 1; perfect interventions are used for the stronger parameter-identifiability theorem.

novelty_flags.label: thm:square-equality
novelty_flags.one_line: Absent a demonstrated assumption-class separation, the square covariance equality is a relabelling/weaker corollary of Squires et al.'s covariance-based graph recovery with injective mixing, rather than a new square frontier.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3-5, Assumptions 1-2, Theorem 1, Proposition 1, and Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 1 specifies generic single-node row changes with p>=d; Theorem 1 says d interventions suffice to recover G from covariance precision matrices under Assumption 1, while Theorem 2 gives graph, target, and parameter identifiability under Assumptions 1 and 2 (perfect interventions).

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.3, Definition 3.14 and Theorem 3.15; Section 5, Problems 5.1-5.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Definition 3.14 defines soft(G) through baseline inverse-path rank equalities; Theorem 3.15 identifies it with the paper's compatibility class; Problems 5.1-5.2 ask for a combinatorial description and whether the stated soft/covariance/same-closure containments are strict.
Theorem 1 identifies the transitive closure under its intervention assumptions, while Theorem 2 identifies the exact causal structure only after its additional adjacency-faithfulness assumption.
The paper derives semialgebraic image descriptions for birational maps under positive-denominator conditions and applies this to globally rationally identifiable statistical models.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct the Squires comparison, then either remove the square-equality theorem as known or prove an explicit non-overlap between its generic B-row model and the proposal's covariance model; the retained-edge condition alone does not do this.
Make the overcomplete p<q positive-real compiler the sole headline, with the fork classification as its exhibited first instance and the terminal-row correction as the independent field-tier theorem.

State a first tractable graph family for the compiler (for example bounded terminal-linkage width), with an explicit branch/certificate complexity bound before claiming the all-graph bit-complexity target.

recommended_next_step: Revise the Squires comparison and square theorem; retain the actual-row correction and overcomplete positive-real compiler as the field-tier kernel.
